users_and_stakeholders.interest: No operating day starts short of passed-out volunteers.

steps: A volunteer e-mails the swaps mailbox.
The roster manager checks the competence register for both volunteers.
The roster manager edits the duty roster spreadsheet.
On gala days the operations manager checks the platform posts again in the morning.
The roster manager replies to both volunteers from the mailbox once the spreadsheet is edited.
problems: On two gala days a platform duty went to a volunteer not passed out for platform work.
Swaps for the same duty sometimes arrive twice and both get accepted.
The register and the roster are checked by one person, so a busy week means mistakes.
cites: [A:A01 "on two gala days a platform duty went to a volunteer not passed out for platform work"]

confidence.high: The row quotes the swap e-mail and the competence register line that decided it, and both name the same post and day.
confidence.medium: A reputable secondary source; not expected here.
confidence.low: Inferred or one weak source, for example a volunteer's own claim to be passed out with no register line; such a swap is refused and raised as a question.

conflicts: The higher rank wins within its own area.

output.description: One row per swap message, with a decision: approve or refuse. A swap that names no operating day or no post is refused as incomplete; a second swap for a duty already swapped is refused as a duplicate.

risk.notes: A wrong swap can be put right before the operating day, but not once the trains are running. Station volunteers and visitors on the platform are affected. Nothing is written to any system: the roster manager edits the spreadsheet after approving, so every decision can still be changed before an operating day. The worst case is a gala day platform without a passed-out volunteer, which the operations manager would have to cover in person. Volunteers who are told a duty is theirs plan their day around it, so a swap that is approved and later withdrawn costs goodwill even when no harm is done.
